$comment: The pin. ADR-0008: content is a versioned artefact of the book, never its source, and
this repository never parses LaTeX (P11). SHARED-SERVICE-REUSE.md §2's rule for an
image applies to content too — pinned, never a moving ref.
Every file below is FETCHED by scripts/fetch-book-content.sh and written under
web/content/book/. None of them is hand-edited here; a change is made in the book and
arrives by moving the pin. The digests are what make that enforceable: the fetch
verifies each file against its digest and fails loudly on a mismatch, so a silently
edited fixture cannot pass for a fetched one.
PROVISIONAL, and stated as such. Phase 2 replaces this file-by-file fetch with the
content bundle the book attaches to a v* release (book issue #239 §1). That bundle
does not exist yet, which is why phase 1 fetches the lab engine directly and why this
is the interim shape rather than the destination.

source.revisionNote: the merge commit of the book's PR #238 — the tree the lab engine was verified on
source.license: the book is CC BY-NC-SA; its lab/ code is MIT. See the book's own LICENSE files.

layoutNote: The relative layout is load-bearing and must be reproduced exactly in the virtual file
system Pyodide mounts. labkit.py computes the repository root as
Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2], so it must sit exactly two directories below the
root, and it then reads <root>/figures/values/<program>.tex and
<root>/lab/<exercises|solutions>/<stem>.py. check.py resolves only its own sibling
tests directory, HERE/'tests'. Flatten any of this and the engine looks for the values
file in the wrong place and fails at import — as a traceback, not as a FAIL line.
